status: Concrete reusable data and helper assertions. Proof status is recorded by the kernel dependency audit; later proof edits require current CI verification.

nodes.title: Explicit moment coefficient data
nodes.statement_tex: A coefficient family assigns a continuous symmetric k-linear form B_k^(j) to every pair of natural indices. IsMomentExpansion(mu,B) requires permutation symmetry and, for every k,q>=1, the operator-norm expansion b_(k,s)=sum_(j=1)^q s^j B_k^(j)/j!+o(s^q) as s decreases to zero through positive values. Degree vanishing and support identities are separate theorems.

nodes.title: Evaluation of the Bochner moment form
nodes.statement_tex: The kernel momentKernel(k,z) evaluates to the product of the inner products with z. If the Gaussian-weighted kernel is Bochner integrable, evaluation of gaussianMomentForm(mu,k,s) at a tuple equals the existing scalar gaussianMoment. The curried second-degree form momentBilinear(A) evaluates at (u,v) as A(u,v).
hypotheses: The weighted multilinear kernel is integrable for the integral-evaluation assertion.

nodes.title: Permutation symmetry of Gaussian moment forms
nodes.statement_tex: For every measure, degree, real Gaussian parameter, permutation sigma of Fin k, and tuple u, b_(k,s)(u composed with sigma)=b_(k,s)(u). The total Bochner definition is symmetric even when its integral takes the default zero value.

nodes.title: A common polynomial growth bound
nodes.statement_tex: HasPolynomialGrowthBound(mu,C,p) means C,p>=0 and mu(closedBall(0,R)) <= ofReal(C(1+R)^p) for every R>0. Families use the same finite real constants C,p.

nodes.title: Trace and restriction of continuous bilinear forms
nodes.statement_tex: For a continuous real bilinear form A on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, bilinearTrace(A) is LinearMap.trace of the endomorphism obtained by Riesz representation. restrictBilinear(A,V) precomposes both variables with the subtype inclusion of V. momentBilinear curries a degree-two continuous multilinear form.

nodes.title: Trace as an orthonormal diagonal sum
nodes.statement_tex: For every finite orthonormal basis e, bilinearTrace(A)=sum_i A(e_i,e_i).

nodes.title: An admissible flatness cutoff
nodes.statement_tex: A continuous compactly supported real function phi is admissible if 0<=phi<=1, phi=1 on the closed unit ball, and its topological support is contained in the open ball of radius two.

nodes.title: Existence of an admissible cutoff
nodes.statement_tex: For every ambient Euclidean dimension there exists an admissible flatness cutoff.

nodes.title: A cutoff flatness gap threshold
nodes.statement_tex: IsFlatnessGap(m,phi,epsilon) means epsilon>0 and every centered unit m-uniform conical measure with cutoff flatness at most epsilon is flat.

nodes.title: Transfer the conical gap to cutoff flatness
nodes.statement_tex: For 1<=m<=n and an admissible cutoff phi, there exists epsilon such that IsFlatnessGap(m,phi,epsilon).

nodes.title: Quantified crossing scale data
nodes.statement_tex: FirstCrossingData records positive sigma_i<=r_i, r_i tending to zero, vague convergence of the r_i blow-ups to alpha and sigma_i blow-ups to xi, energy exactly epsilon at every sigma_i and at xi, and energy at most epsilon on every entire interval [sigma_i,r_i]. Divergence of r_i/sigma_i and flatness at infinity are separate theorems.

nodes.title: Continuity, homogeneity, and norm bound of moment kernels
nodes.statement_tex: The map z to momentKernel(k,z) is continuous, momentKernel(k,a z)=a^k momentKernel(k,z) for every real scalar a, and its operator norm equals norm(z)^k. The upper-bound lemma remains independently available. These assertions hold in every natural degree, including zero.

nodes.title: Integrability from summable annulus bounds
nodes.statement_tex: Let mu be a Borel measure on an arbitrary proper normed additive group E with finite mass on every positive-radius closed ball centered at zero. Let f be continuous and normed-additive-group valued. For nonnegative constants M_j, suppose norm(f(x))<=M_j whenever j<=norm(x)<=j+1. If sum_j M_j mu(closedBall(0,j+1)) is summable, then f is Bochner integrable.

nodes.title: Integral bound from a countable measurable cover
nodes.statement_tex: For any measure on any measurable space, a nonnegative integrable real function f, measurable sets S_j, and a summable real sequence B_j bounding integral_(S_j) f, the integral of f on the union of the S_j is at most sum_j B_j. Disjointification removes any overlap of the cover.

nodes.title: A summable common Gaussian annulus majorant
nodes.statement_tex: For C>=0, arbitrary real p, a natural degree d, and s>0, the sequence B_j=(j+1)^d exp(-s j^2) C(j+2)^p is summable. Bound the polynomial factor using ceil(p), use j^2>=j for natural j, and compare with a polynomial times the geometric series exp(-s)^j.

nodes.title: Gaussian integrals on unit annuli
nodes.statement_tex: If C>=0 and mu(closedBall(0,R))<=ofReal(C(1+R)^p) for all R>0, then for every natural j,d and s>0, the integral of norm(z)^d exp(-s norm(z)^2) over j<=norm(z)<=j+1 is at most (j+1)^d exp(-s j^2) C(j+2)^p. No regularity assumption is needed.

nodes.title: A common series controls every Gaussian tail
nodes.statement_tex: Under the same polynomial ball bound with C>=0, for every natural N and real R>=N, the Gaussian-polynomial integral outside closedBall(0,R) is at most sum_(j>=0) B_(j+N), where B_l=(l+1)^d exp(-s l^2) C(l+2)^p. The majorant is independent of the measure.

nodes.title: Integrability of all polynomial Gaussian weights
nodes.statement_tex: For a measure mu on Euclidean n with mu(closedBall(0,R))<=ofReal(C(1+R)^p) at every R>0, where C>=0 and p is real, every multivariate real polynomial P, natural d, and s>0 satisfy Bochner integrability of norm(z)^d P(z) exp(-s norm(z)^2). The proof inducts on P using closure under constants, addition, and multiplication by a coordinate; norm(z_i)<=norm(z) supplies the inductive domination.

nodes.title: Weighted ball scaling for conical measures
nodes.statement_tex: For a conical measure $\mu$ and a measurable real-valued function $h$ homogeneous of arbitrary real degree $a$, for every $r>0$, $\int_{\overline B(0,r)}h\,d\mu=r^{m+a}\int_{\overline B(0,1)}h\,d\mu$. No positivity or integrability assumption is needed for this scaling identity; both sides use the Bochner nonintegrable-value convention. Under the same scaling hypotheses, integrability of h on the unit closed ball implies integrability on every positive-radius closed ball.
nodes.source: Direct change of variables in the conical scaling identity; reusable supporting lemma for De Lellis homogeneous radial integration.

nodes.title: Small covers from a lower ball bound
nodes.statement_tex: Let $X$ be a separable metric Borel space, $A\subseteq U$ with $U$ open, and $a,R>0$. Assume $a r^m\leq\mu(B(x,r))$ for all $x\in A$ and $0<r<R$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a countable cover of $A$ by fivefold enlargements of disjoint balls in $U$, each enlarged ball having diameter at most $\varepsilon$, and total diameter-to-the-$m$ cost at most $(10^m/a)\mu(U)$.
nodes.source: Vitali fivefold covering and outer regularity; locally kernel-checked.

nodes.title: Lower ball bounds control Hausdorff measure in open supersets
nodes.statement_tex: Under the lower ball bound above, $\mathcal H^m(A)\leq (10^m/a)\mu(U)$ for every open superset $U$ of $A$. No measurability of $A$ or regularity of $\mu$ is needed.
nodes.source: Vitali fivefold covering and outer regularity; locally kernel-checked.

nodes.title: Hausdorff comparison by outer regularity
nodes.statement_tex: If $\mu$ is outer regular and the same uniform lower ball bound holds at every point of an arbitrary set $A$, then $\mathcal H^m(A)\leq (10^m/a)\mu(A)$.
nodes.source: Vitali fivefold covering and outer regularity; locally kernel-checked.

nodes.title: Restricted lower ball comparison
nodes.statement_tex: For a Borel stratum $S$ and an outer regular measure satisfying the uniform lower ball bound at every point of $S$, $\mathcal H^m\!\restriction S\leq (10^m/a)\mu\!\restriction S$.
nodes.source: Vitali fivefold covering and outer regularity; locally kernel-checked.

nodes.title: Support under homeomorphisms and nonzero scalar multiplication
nodes.statement_tex: For a homeomorphism $e:X\to Y$ of Borel topological spaces and any measure $\mu$ on $X$, $\operatorname{spt}(e_\#\mu)=e(\operatorname{spt}\mu)$. For a measure on any topological measurable space and any $c\in[0,\infty]$ with $c\ne0$, $\operatorname{spt}(c\mu)=\operatorname{spt}\mu$. Neither assertion requires regularity or local finiteness.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The source and target Borel structures agree with their topologies for the homeomorphism assertion. The scalar assertion needs only topological and measurable structures and $c\ne0$.
nodes.source: Direct transport of the open-neighborhood characterization of support.

nodes.title: Support and regularity of dimensional blow-ups
nodes.statement_tex: For every $m,n\in\mathbb N$, measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$, point $a$, and radius $r>0$, the dimensional blow-up $\mu_{a,r}=r^{-m}(T_{a,r})_\#\mu$ has support $T_{a,r}(\operatorname{spt}\mu)$, where $T_{a,r}(y)=(y-a)/r$. If $\mu$ is regular, then $\mu_{a,r}$ is regular.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The radius is strictly positive. Regularity of $\mu$ is required only for the regularity conclusion; the support identity holds for every measure.
nodes.source: Homeomorphic affine transport, nonzero finite scalar normalization, and mathlib regularity under maps and scalar multiplication.

nodes.title: Rational good sets from positive finite density bounds
nodes.statement_tex: If $0<\Theta_*^m(\mu,x)$ and $\Theta^{m,*}(\mu,x)<\infty$, then there are positive rational numbers $p,q$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $0<r<1/(k+1)$, $p r^m\leq\mu(\overline B(x,r))\leq q r^m$. Equivalently, $x\in\mathrm{goodSet}(m,p,q,k,\mu)$ using the existing FormalizingGMT definition.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: $m,n\in\mathbb N$, $\mu$ is a measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and the lower and upper densities obey the displayed positive finite bounds. A density limit and local finiteness are not required.
nodes.source: Choose a positive real number below RatioOfDensities and apply FormalizingGMT.exists_goodSet_mem.

nodes.title: Exact blow-up invariance of flat plane measures
nodes.statement_tex: For an $m$-plane $V$, every scalar $c\in[0,\infty]$, every $x\in V$, and $r>0$, $D^m_{x,r}(c\,\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V)=c\,\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V$. This includes $m=0$ and does not require $c$ positive or finite.

nodes.title: Nonnegativity of distance energy and flatness
nodes.statement_tex: For every nonnegative compactly supported continuous cutoff and every measure, the squared-distance energy of every plane is nonnegative, and so is its infimum defining flatness. No regularity or minimizing-plane theorem is needed; when the plane type is empty, the real infimum convention gives zero.

nodes.title: Vanishing distance energy on a supporting plane
nodes.statement_tex: The squared-distance energy on $V$ of $c\,\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V$ is zero for any scalar $c\in[0,\infty]$. Consequently every flat measure has zero flatness for every nonnegative cutoff, without regularity or existence of a global minimizer.

nodes.title: Gaussian integral from a centered power ball law
nodes.statement_tex: For an s-finite positive measure $\rho$ on a normed additive commutative group with its Borel measurable structure, $C\geq0$, and $d>0$, if $\rho(\overline B(0,r))=Cr^d$ for every $r>0$, then $e^{-\|z\|^2}$ is integrable and its integral is $C\Gamma(d/2+1)$. The centered ball law suffices.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: Write $e^{-\|z\|^2}=\int_{\|z\|^2}^{\infty}e^{-t}\,dt$. Nonnegative Fubini gives $\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\rho(\overline B(0,\sqrt t))\,dt$. Substitute the ball law and use the Gamma integral. Finiteness of this nonnegative integral gives Bochner integrability.

nodes.title: The nonnegative exponential tail integral
nodes.statement_tex: For every real a, the Lebesgue lintegral of ofReal(exp(-t)) over Ici(a) equals ofReal(exp(-a)).

nodes.title: Lower density from a lower power bound
nodes.statement_tex: Let $\mu$ be an outer measure on a pseudometric space, $m\in\mathbb N$, $a\geq0$, and $R>0$. If $\mu(B(x,r))\geq a r^m$ for every $0<r<R$, then $\Theta_*^m(\mu,x)\geq a/2^m$. The factor $2^m$ comes from the diameter-normalized definition of density.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Only an outer measure, a pseudometric space, $a\geq0$, and $R>0$ are required. No measurability, local finiteness, or density-limit hypothesis is used.
nodes.source: Closed-ball inclusion and an eventual lower bound for the liminf of the density ratios.

nodes.title: All exponential moments make power moments determining
nodes.statement_tex: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real functions on arbitrary measure spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Omega^\prime,\nu)$. Suppose $\exp(tX)$ and $\exp(tY)$ are integrable for every real $t$. If $\int X^k\,d\mu=\int Y^k\,d\nu$ for every natural $k$, then their complex moment generating functions agree at every complex argument.
hypotheses: Arbitrary measurable source spaces; no probability normalization is assumed.
Every real exponential parameter is integrable for each function.
All natural power moments, including order zero, agree.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: Exponential integrability makes both complex moment generating functions entire. Their iterated derivatives at zero equal the power moments, hence the canonical power series agree. Local power-series uniqueness and analytic continuation give equality everywhere.

nodes.title: Gaussian weighting gives a finite measure
nodes.statement_tex: If $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ obeys $\operatorname{HasPolynomialGrowthBound}(\mu,C,p)$, then the measure $e^{-\|z\|^2}\mu$ is finite.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: Degree-zero Gaussian integrability identifies the total mass of the weighted measure with a finite real integral.

nodes.title: Every projection has all exponential moments after Gaussian weighting
nodes.statement_tex: If $\operatorname{HasPolynomialGrowthBound}(\mu,C,p)$, then for every $w\in\mathbb R^n$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, the function $e^{-\|z\|^2}e^{t\langle z,w\rangle}$ is $\mu$-integrable. Equivalently, $e^{t\langle z,w\rangle}$ is integrable for the Gaussian weighted measure.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: Cauchy--Schwarz and a completed square give $t\langle z,w\rangle-\|z\|^2\leq |t|^2\|w\|^2/2-\|z\|^2/2$. The right side supplies an integrable Gaussian majorant with rate $1/2$. The withDensity integrability identity gives the weighted formulation.

nodes.title: Existence of a plane in every admissible dimension
nodes.statement_tex: If $m\leq n$, the type of $m$-dimensional linear subspaces of $\mathbb R^n$ is nonempty. Choose $m$ linearly independent vectors and take their span.

nodes.title: Continuity of projection energy
nodes.statement_tex: The distance energy of a plane is the integral of $\varphi(z)|z-P_Vz|^2$. For any compactly supported continuous $\varphi$ and any measure finite on compact sets, the same integral is a continuous function of an arbitrary continuous linear operator $P$.

nodes.title: Minimizing flatness under finiteness on compact sets
nodes.statement_tex: For $m\leq n$, every compactly supported continuous real cutoff and every measure finite on compact sets admit a plane attaining the infimum of distance energy. The cutoff need not be nonnegative. Minimize the continuous operator energy over the compact set of rank-$m$ orthogonal projections.

nodes.title: Integrability of compactly weighted distance energy
nodes.statement_tex: For every compactly supported continuous real cutoff, every plane, and every measure finite on compact sets, the cutoff times squared distance to the plane is integrable.

nodes.title: Continuous finite ball profiles have null spheres
nodes.statement_tex: Let $\mu$ be a Borel measure on a pseudometric space, $x$ a point, and $r>0$. Suppose a real function $f$ is continuous at $r$ and $\mu(\overline B(x,s))=\operatorname{ofReal}(f(s))$ for every $s>0$. Then $B(x,r)=\overline B(x,r)$ almost everywhere, the sphere of radius $r$ has measure zero, and every normed real vector-valued Bochner integrand has equal integrals on the open and closed balls.
hypotheses: PseudoMetricSpace X, MeasurableSpace X, BorelSpace X.
The entire positive-radius closed-ball profile is finite and represented by f; f is continuous only at the radius r under consideration.
The Bochner integral equality requires no additional integrability assumption.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: Approach r through smaller positive radii. Monotonicity bounds each smaller closed-ball mass by the open-ball mass, and continuity gives the reverse inequality to ball inclusion. Finiteness yields almost-everywhere equality and zero measure of the boundary. Equality of restricted measures gives equality of total Bochner integrals.

nodes.title: Open and closed uniform balls agree almost everywhere
nodes.statement_tex: For every unit $m$-uniform measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$, support center $x$, and positive radius $r$, $B(x,r)=\overline B(x,r)$ almost everywhere for $\mu$. This includes $m=0$.

nodes.title: Derivative of a product with the identity at zero
nodes.statement_tex: For every positive natural $n$ and every real function $f$ that is $C^n$ at zero, $D^n(t\mapsto t f(t))(0)=nD^{n-1}f(0)$.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: In Leibniz's finite sum, only the first derivative of the identity contributes at zero.

nodes.title: All even derivatives of a quadratic exponential
nodes.statement_tex: For every real $a$ and natural $j$, $D^{2j}(t\mapsto e^{at^2/2})(0)=\frac{(2j)!}{2^j j!}a^j$. No sign restriction on $a$ is required.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: The differential equation $f'(t)=atf(t)$ gives the recurrence $D^{2j+2}f(0)=a(2j+1)D^{2j}f(0)$. Induction and the factorial recurrence give the formula.

nodes.statement_tex: For every nonnegative real variance $v$, including zero, and every natural $j$, $\int x^{2j}\,d\mathcal N(0,v)=\frac{(2j)!}{2^j j!}v^j$.

nodes.title: Integrability of finite products of Gaussian projections
nodes.statement_tex: For a standard Gaussian on any finite dimensional real inner product space $E$, every natural power of a real linear projection is integrable. For every finite index type $I$ and vectors $(u_i)_{i\in I}$, the function $x\mapsto\prod_i\langle u_i,x\rangle$ is integrable, including the empty product. A four-projection companion is also provided.
nodes.proof_sketch_tex: Fernique's theorem supplies all finite norm moments. The product is bounded in norm by $(\prod_i\|u_i\|)\|x\|^{|I|}$; measurability and domination give integrability.

nodes.title: Detecting convergence by further subsequences
nodes.statement_tex: A sequence in a pseudometric space converges to $x$ if every strictly increasing subsequence has a further strictly increasing subsequence converging to $x$.

nodes.title: Moving projection energies under vague convergence
nodes.statement_tex: Let $\mu_i\rightharpoonup\nu$ be regular Euclidean measures, $P_i\to P$ in operator norm, and $\varphi$ a compactly supported continuous real function. Then $\int\varphi(z)|z-P_i z|^2\,d\mu_i\to\int\varphi(z)|z-Pz|^2\,d\nu$. Operators need not be projections and the cutoff need not be nonnegative.

nodes.title: Vague continuity of minimum energy for general cutoffs
nodes.statement_tex: For $m\leq n$, every compactly supported continuous real cutoff has vaguely continuous minimum squared-distance energy on regular measures. Extract convergent minimizing projections along every subsequence, use the moving-integral lemma, and compare with a fixed minimizing plane for the limit measure. No nonnegativity or special cutoff normalization is needed.

nodes.title: Measure bounds from eventual membership in moving sets
nodes.statement_tex: Let $S_i,T\subseteq X$ and $c\in[0,\infty]$. If eventually $\mu(S_i)\le c$ and every $x\in T$ eventually belongs to $S_i$, then $\mu(T)\le c$. If $\mu$ is finite, each $S_i$ is $\mu$-null-measurable, eventually $c\le\mu(S_i)$, and every $x\notin T$ is eventually outside $S_i$, then $c\le\mu(T)$.
hypotheses: An arbitrary measurable space and measure; the second assertion additionally assumes a finite measure and null-measurable moving sets. No measurability of the target set is required.

nodes.title: Distance to a subspace through orthogonal projection
nodes.statement_tex: In a real or complex inner-product space, let $V$ be a linear subspace admitting an orthogonal projection $P_V$. For every $x$, $\operatorname{dist}(x,V)=\lVert x-P_Vx\rVert$.
hypotheses: A real or complex inner-product space; the subspace admits an orthogonal projection.

nodes.title: Convergent subsequences of fixed-rank plane projections
nodes.statement_tex: For every sequence of $m$-planes $V_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, there exist an $m$-plane $V$ and a strictly increasing $\phi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that $P_{V_{\phi(i)}}\to P_V$ in operator norm.
hypotheses: A sequence of linear subspaces of the same prescribed finite dimension in Euclidean space.

nodes.title: Countable-test vague metric specification
nodes.statement_tex: A regular Euclidean measure is a positive Borel measure equipped with regularity. A vague metrization consists of compactly supported continuous tests $f_j$, a metric on these measures whose distance is $\sum_{j\geq0}2^{-(j+1)}\min(1,|\int f_j\,d\mu-\int f_j\,d\nu|)$, cutoff tests majorizing $1$ on each positive-radius closed ball and nonnegative everywhere, and equivalence between metric sequential convergence and vague convergence for every sequence of regular measures.
hypotheses: n : Nat
The metric and all of its specifications are explicit fields; the definition chooses no data from an existence theorem.
nodes.status_note: Definitions contain no placeholders. This is data/specification, not a claim that such data exist.

nodes.title: Consequences of a supplied vague metric
nodes.statement_tex: For supplied $M:\mathrm{VagueMetrization}(n)$, metric convergence is equivalent to vague convergence; its countable-test distance separates measures; and every compact family has a finite cover by metric balls of every positive radius, with centers in that family.
hypotheses: M : VagueMetrization n is supplied explicitly.
The finite-cover conclusion assumes the family is compact in M.metric.

nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Gaussian moment continuity under vague convergence
nodes.statement_tex: Along vaguely convergent unit-uniform measures, every Gaussian multilinear moment evaluated on fixed vectors converges at every positive Gaussian parameter.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Taylor coefficients of an exactly homogeneous moment
nodes.statement_tex: If a positive-degree Gaussian moment is exactly $s^d A$, its Taylor coefficient family has only one nonzero positive-order coefficient, equal to $d!A$ in degree $d$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Sparse moment coefficients of conical measures
nodes.statement_tex: For a positive-dimensional conical unit-uniform measure, $B_k^j$ vanishes unless $k=2j$; in that degree it equals $j!$ times the moment at parameter one.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Even Gaussian moments at support points
nodes.statement_tex: For a positive-dimensional conical unit-uniform measure and $x$ in its support, the degree $2j$ diagonal moment at parameter one equals $\lVert x\rVert^{2j}/j!$ for every $j>0$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: A symmetric multilinear form is determined by its diagonal
nodes.statement_tex: A continuous symmetric multilinear map over real normed spaces is zero if all its diagonal evaluations vanish. This includes degree zero and requires neither finite dimension nor completeness.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Weighted plane energy in orthonormal coordinates
nodes.statement_tex: An integrable weighted squared distance to a subspace equals the weighted squared norm integral minus the sum of directional second moments.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Leading covariance eigenspaces minimize plane energy
nodes.statement_tex: Given an ordered spectral representation of the weighted covariance, the plane spanned by its first $m$ eigenvectors minimizes weighted squared distance among all $m$-planes.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Gaussian bilinear covariance identities
nodes.statement_tex: The degree-two Gaussian moment defines a symmetric bilinear form. Its diagonal equals twice the Gaussian directional second moment divided by Gaussian mass, with directional integrability following from moment-kernel integrability.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Normalized flat measures are conical
nodes.statement_tex: The normalized Hausdorff measure on a linear plane is invariant under dimensional dilations.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Zero-dimensional flat measures and their moments
nodes.statement_tex: A normalized zero-dimensional flat measure is the Dirac mass at the origin. Its zeroth moment is one and every positive-degree moment vanishes, including the required projected even-moment formula.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Flat moments depend only on projected vectors
nodes.statement_tex: Diagonal Gaussian moments of a normalized flat measure are unchanged by orthogonal projection of their argument to the plane. The zeroth moment equals one at every positive Gaussian parameter.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Unit-uniform measures are nonzero
nodes.statement_tex: A unit-uniform measure is nonzero because its support contains the origin.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Existence and uniformity of tangents at infinity
nodes.statement_tex: A positive-dimensional unit-uniform measure admits a tangent at infinity, and every such tangent remains unit-uniform.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of tangents at infinity
nodes.statement_tex: Any two tangents at infinity of a positive-dimensional unit-uniform measure agree, by equality of their Gaussian polynomial moments.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Leading homogeneous terms along escaping sequences
nodes.statement_tex: For a finite sum of continuous multilinear homogeneous polynomials, dividing its values at $r_i y_i$ by the highest power of $r_i$ yields the leading diagonal value when $r_i\to\infty$ and $y_i\to v$. Nonnegativity on those points implies nonnegativity of the leading value.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Conical Gaussian energy and unit-ball energy
nodes.statement_tex: For a conical unit-uniform measure, Gaussian squared-distance energy equals unit-ball squared-distance energy times the corresponding Gamma factor.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Gaussian norm moments bounded by half-scale mass
nodes.statement_tex: An integrable Gaussian norm moment of positive degree $k$ is bounded by $(k/s)^{k/2}$ times the Gaussian mass at parameter $s/2$, for any measure on a real normed additive group.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Normalized Gaussian norm bounds for uniform measures
nodes.statement_tex: For positive-dimensional unit-uniform measures, halving the Gaussian parameter scales its mass by $2^{m/2}$. Dividing Gaussian norm moments by Gaussian mass gives an explicit bound of order $s^{-k/2}$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Coefficient vanishing from growth of linear images
nodes.statement_tex: If a continuous linear image of a positive-degree Gaussian moment is $O(s^a)$, every positive Taylor coefficient of degree $j<a$ has zero image. Fixed-vector evaluation is a specialization.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Continuous trace of moments on a subspace
nodes.statement_tex: Tracing a degree-two moment on a subspace is a continuous linear functional. On the moment kernel it equals the squared norm of orthogonal projection.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Subspace Gaussian trace under a cylinder identity
nodes.statement_tex: The subspace trace of the Gaussian second moment is an explicit integral of squared projection. If that squared projection equals $2\langle b,z\rangle$ almost everywhere, the trace equals $2s$ times the first moment evaluated at $b$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Taylor coefficients after multiplication by scale
nodes.statement_tex: If $f(s)=sa+o(s)$, $g(s)=sb+s^2c/2+o(s^2)$, and $g(s)=dsf(s)$ near zero through positive values, then $b=0$ and $c=2da$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Bounded holes in a plane near a uniform support
nodes.statement_tex: If the support of an $m$-dimensional unit-uniform measure lies in a bounded tube around an $m$-plane, every point of that plane lies within a uniform finite distance of the support.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Taylor remainders under scalar linear maps
nodes.statement_tex: Applying a continuous real linear functional to a Gaussian moment preserves its Taylor remainder estimate and applies the same functional to every coefficient.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Second coefficient trace from a cylinder identity
nodes.statement_tex: For a positive-dimensional unit-uniform measure satisfying the quadratic cylinder identity almost everywhere, the subspace trace of $B_2^2$ equals $4B_1^1(b)$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Trace splits over orthogonal complementary subspaces
nodes.statement_tex: The trace of any continuous real bilinear form on a finite-dimensional inner-product space equals the sum of its traces restricted to a subspace and its orthogonal complement.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Scalar Gaussian moments from product growth
nodes.statement_tex: If the product of the degree-$k$ evaluation functionals is bounded almost everywhere by $C\lVert z\rVert^d$, its Gaussian moment is $O(s^{k-d/2})$. Zero degrees are included.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Cubic coefficients with two normal inputs vanish
nodes.statement_tex: For a unit-uniform measure whose support lies in a bounded tube around a subspace, $B_3^2(v,w,w)=0$ whenever $w$ is normal to that subspace and $v$ is arbitrary.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Binomial formula for a symmetric trilinear form
nodes.statement_tex: The diagonal of a continuous symmetric real trilinear form at $x+y$ expands with coefficients $1,3,3,1$ into its pure and mixed evaluations.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Leading coefficient from a little-o remainder
nodes.statement_tex: A normed-space-valued function equal to $s^j a+o(s^j)$ converges to $a$ after division by $s^j$ as $s$ tends to zero through positive values.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Vanishing of scaled normalized bounded integrals
nodes.statement_tex: For any nonnegative integrable weights with positive mass, the weighted average of an essentially bounded function tends to zero after multiplication by a positive scale tending to zero.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: A convergent function has no nonzero scaled derivative limit
nodes.statement_tex: If $f(s)$ converges to a finite real limit and $s f\prime(s)$ has a finite limit as $s\downarrow0$, that scaled derivative limit is zero. The proof uses the quotient $(sf(s))/s$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Rigidity forms from symmetric coefficient tensors
nodes.statement_tex: Symmetric second and third coefficient forms determine the required normal-valued bilinear map and adjusted scalar bilinear form through Riesz representation. No measure or tangent assumption is required.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Quadratic bound from bounded offsets
nodes.statement_tex: If $y_i\to v$, $\lVert q_i\rVert\le B$ eventually, and $A(y_i,y_i)+\langle\omega(y_i,y_i),q_i\rangle\to0$, then $A(v,v)^2\le B^2\lVert\omega(v,v)\rVert^2$. The spaces and continuous bilinear maps are arbitrary.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Gaussian integrals of functions with linear growth
nodes.statement_tex: A measurable function bounded almost everywhere by $C(1+\lVert z\rVert)$ is Gaussian integrable whenever Gaussian mass and first norm moment are integrable, with the corresponding explicit integral bound.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Vanishing of scaled Gaussian linear-growth averages
nodes.statement_tex: For a positive-dimensional unit-uniform measure, the Gaussian integral of a linearly bounded measurable function, multiplied by $s$ and divided by Gaussian mass, tends to zero as $s\downarrow0$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Scalar lower bound from a quadratic inequality
nodes.statement_tex: If $d>0$, $q\ge0$, and $(1+2/d)t^2\le-8qt$, then $t\ge-8dq/(d+2)$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Gaussian trace lower bound from a squared-form upper bound
nodes.statement_tex: For a symmetric bilinear form on a positive-dimensional real inner-product space, a Gaussian squared-form bound by $-8q$ times its mean forces the mean to be at least $-8dq/(d+2)$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Difference of bilinear diagonal values
nodes.statement_tex: For a continuous bilinear map, $\lVert Q(z,z)-Q(p,p)\rVert\le\lVert Q\rVert\lVert z-p\rVert(\lVert z\rVert+\lVert p\rVert)$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of regular vague limits
nodes.statement_tex: Two regular measures that are vague limits of the same sequence agree.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Flatness transfers between tangent normalizations
nodes.statement_tex: Under positive finite density bounds, a flat tangent yields a flat dimensional tangent, and flatness of all dimensional tangents yields flatness of all tangents. A common positive finite scalar normalization can be undone.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Positive finite density under scalar multiplication
nodes.statement_tex: Multiplication of a measure by a positive finite scalar preserves positive finite existing dimensional density.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Integrability of squared norms of Gaussian bilinear diagonals
nodes.statement_tex: The squared norm of a continuous Hilbert-valued bilinear form evaluated diagonally is integrable under standard Gaussian measure on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Vector-valued Gaussian fourth moment with zero mean
nodes.statement_tex: For a symmetric Hilbert-valued bilinear form with zero Gaussian mean, its Gaussian squared norm equals twice the sum of squared norms of its matrix entries in an orthonormal basis.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Gaussian means and contractions of vector bilinear forms
nodes.statement_tex: The Gaussian mean of a vector-valued bilinear diagonal is its basis trace. Zero mean implies zero scalar component means and the corresponding factor-two weighted Gaussian contraction.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Polarization of weighted integral limits
nodes.statement_tex: Integrability and convergence of weighted diagonal square integrals imply their cross-product counterparts by polarization. This applies to diagonal limits of Hilbert-valued bilinear forms.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Finite-basis bilinear expansion and integral limits
nodes.statement_tex: A bilinear diagonal expands in a finite orthonormal basis. Eventual integrability and limits of finitely many weighted integrals pass through their fixed linear combinations.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: First and second scaled moment limits
nodes.statement_tex: For every positive moment degree, division by $s$ yields the first coefficient in the limit. If that coefficient vanishes, division by $s^2$ yields half the second coefficient.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Centered mixed Gaussian limit from Taylor coefficients
nodes.statement_tex: The normalized centered cubic Gaussian integral converges to $3B_3^2(v,v,w)-4B_2^1(v,v)\langle b,w\rangle$.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.

nodes.title: Centered Gaussian mean from its first coefficient
nodes.statement_tex: If $B_1^1(w)=2\langle b,w\rangle$, the normalized Gaussian average of $\langle z-b,w\rangle$ tends to zero.
nodes.verification: Independent kernel check passed with standard foundations; canonical integration CI pending.
